text:
sarah.k: Quick follow-up to the telemetry-split RFC — I want to propose extracting metrics/tracing ingestion out of the model workers into a lightweight sidecar. Goal is to decouple export logic, reduce per-service deps, and make rollouts independent.

mike.t: +1 in principle. we spiked this last quarter. main wins were faster deploys for the model service and fewer thorny lib upgrades. main drawbacks: extra memory per pod and risk of request-path amplification if sidecar blocks.

lee: For the spike we pushed a small aggregator in the sidecar to batch spans/metrics. that helped with throughput to vendor backends. measured ~3-6ms added p50 for sync routes, but async routes showed net improvement due to CPU freed on main process.

vicky: Ops checklist: sidecar must have a sensible retry/backoff, circuit-breaker, and a health endpoint. also need egress tags for billing and egress TLS. otherwise we'll have surprise costs and noisy failures.

mike.t: Proposed rollout plan: 1) enable sidecar on playground/non-prod, 2) canary 10% on low-traffic routes (embeddings/async), 3) 50% + baseline perf comparison, 4) switch over if no regressions. fallback: if sidecar fails, route to in-process exporter.

sarah.k: can we capture the fallback behavior in a config flag? something like: 
```yaml
telemetry:
  mode: sidecar  # sidecar | inprocess | hybrid
  sidecar:
    health_check: /healthz
    local_batch_ms: 50
    fallback_on_fail: true
```
That way teams can opt-in per-deployment.

vicky: Also add a per-pod rate limiter and a max-buffer-bytes setting so a noisy pod can't OOM or drown the exporter.

lee: Implementation note: keep sidecar stateless except for short-lived buffers. if we need durable buffering, push to an internal queue service rather than the pod.

mike.t: One tradeoff we should call out in the RFC: prefix/KV cache ownership for traces/metrics. if other services need to annotate spans at send time we need a small API between app and sidecar. I suggest a minimal UDP-like non-blocking UDP/gRPC shim with best-effort semantics.

sarah.k: Good point. propose a one-way non-blocking gRPC client with a 1ms deadline in hot paths. app can opt into blocking calls for critical spans.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for telemetry-sidecar on staging (canary id: cs-202403).

vicky: Please add docs for runbook: how to force inprocess, how to inspect sidecar metrics, and steps to disable egress if vendor has incident.

lee: Suggest adding a small smoke test in CI that validates sidecar health + ability to forward a test span. we had a regression once where sidecar env var was flipped and nothing exported for 48h. :/

sarah.k: OK i'll update the RFC with perf numbers, cost delta estimate (ram + network), and a compact API sketch. assigning @mike.t to timeline spike and @vicky to ops checklist. will tag you for review in the doc in a few hours. :thumbsup:
